name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing patch updates across multiple maintained branches simultaneously. The latest release is v0.61.1 (Open Source) / v1.61.1 (Enterprise), published on May 14, 2025. Multiple version branches (54.x through 61.x) are receiving concurrent patch releases, indicating long-term support across several major versions. Full changelogs are linked per release at https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases but individual diff details were not included in the provided changelog text.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple patch releases across several version branches as recently as May 14, 2025
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud (managed cloud) is available at metabase.com
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, SQLite, MongoDB, Druid, Oracle, Presto/Trino, Spark SQL, and more via drivers

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Tableau offers more advanced visualizations and enterprise features but is a costly proprietary solution compared to Metabase's open-source model.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Lightdash integrates natively with dbt for a metrics-as-code workflow, making it more developer-centric than Metabase's self-service business-user focus.
